To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the early stages of recovery from fasting involve an inter-organ communication between muscle and bone, and that the reactivation of the GH/IGF system is a key factor in the refeeding response.

the refeeding of gilthead sea brean juveniles after 21 days fasting provokes a fast response in the expression of the GH/IGF system and the TOR/AKT pathway, which leads to a recovery of the muscle and bone remodeling.

(a) the muscle and bone remodeling in gilthead seabream juveniles is regulated by the Gh-Igf system, the ubiquitin-proteolytic system and the myogenic regulatory factors; (b) the muscle and the bone remodeling is coordinated by myostatin; and (c) the muscle and osteoclast remodeling are regulated by the Akt-TOR pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular mechanisms involved in the remodeling of the musculoskeletal systems of fish during refeeding after a fasting period.
the identification of the mechanisms involved in the regulation of skeletal muscle and bone growth and remodeling during refeeding.

the identification of genes involved in the regulation of muscle and bone growth during refeeding in fish, which is an important issue in the development of strategies to increase the growth and quality of fish.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
refeeding is a complex process that involves the activation of the GH/IGF system and the activation of the PI3K/Akt pathway that regulates the muscle and bone remodeling.

during refeeding, the muscle tissue recovers its size and strength through the activation of the GH-IGF axis, and the bone recovers its size, strength, and mineralization through the activation of IGFs, GH, and other growth factors.

refeeding is characterized by a rapid recovery of the expression of the Gh/Igfs and myostatin genes in both muscle and bone, followed by a recovery of the expression levels of the other studied genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the muscle and bone remodeling in refeeding is a coordinated process in which the muscle is the first to respond and the bone is second.
refeeding in g. sea bream is a process of recovery of muscle and bone tissue, with the muscle tissue showing a more rapid response than the bone, and with a coordinated inter-organ regulation.

the muscle and bone remodeling in refeeding fish is regulated by a coordinated action between the Gh/Igf, Tor, and Akt signaling pathways, which are also involved in the regulation of myogenesis, myostatin expression, and osteoblastic and osteoclastic differentiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regulation of the Gh/Igfs, Akt, Tor, and mstn2 genes is involved in the recovery of muscle mass and bone remodeling during the early stage of refeeding in gillhead sea bream.
